title: P2: test_density_8_or_below_uses_hash has off-by-one permissive upper bound
description:
**File:** python/tests/test_channel_plan.py
**Line:** 229

**Bug:** The assertion `assert ch <= EU868.num_channels` is too permissive. For EU868 (8 channels), valid channel indices from the hash formula `1 + (h % (n_channels - 1))` are [1, 7], but the test allows up to 8.

**Impact:** If the implementation had an off-by-one bug that returned 8, this test would pass, but later code calling `frequency(8)` would raise ValueError (valid indices are 0-7).

**Fix:** Change to `assert ch < EU868.num_channels` or `assert ch <= EU868.num_channels - 1`

**Severity:** P2 - test weakness that could mask an implementation bug

Tags: codereview, test, P2
close_reason: Bug already fixed. Line 228 of python/tests/test_channel_plan.py now uses `assert ch < EU868.num_channels` (correct strict upper bound) instead of the buggy `assert ch <= EU868.num_channels` that was originally committed. The fix also updated the comment from 'channels are numbered 1..N' to 'CH0 is reserved; data channels are 1..N-1' to accurately reflect the hash formula semantics.
